title: Mercy at every door
hookLine: every surah but one opens with mercy, and mercy is the first name after Allah

lines: A NEW SURAH, A DECORATED PANEL.
cards: Flip through a printed Qur'an. Every few pages a decorated panel announces a new surah's name, and right under it, one line, the same line, again and again. Bismillahi r-rahmani r-rahim.
In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. One hundred fourteen surahs. Count the doors as you go, and you'll find the line over all of them but one.
And you'll find it once more, in a place you wouldn't expect.

teach.h: 113 DOORS, AND ONE IN A LETTER.
teach.b: The bismillah heads one hundred thirteen surahs. Surah nine, at-Tawbah, has none, and scholars give more than one reason.
A report in at-Tirmidhi has the caliph 'Uthman saying it was unclear whether at-Tawbah was its own surah or the continuation of al-Anfal before it, so no line was placed between.
Others said a surah opening with a stern declaration doesn't start with that line. Then the unexpected place.

In surah twenty-seven, the Queen of Sheba opens a letter from Sulayman, and it begins: in the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. So the line still appears one hundred fourteen times. Not one is lost.

teach.h: R-H-M: THE ROOT OF THE WOMB.
teach.b: After Allah, the first two names are ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim, both from the root r-h-m. And rahim, with a slightly different vowel, is the word for a womb.
A hadith qudsi in Abu Dawud has Allah saying: I am ar-Rahman; I created the womb and gave it a name from My name. Mercy, in Arabic, sounds like where everyone began.

Another hadith, in al-Bukhari and Muslim, says Allah divided mercy into a hundred parts and sent one part to earth. From that one part, creatures are kind to each other, so that a mare lifts her hoof away from her foal.
Ninety-nine are kept for the Day. And surah seven: "My mercy embraceth all things." Whatever comes after, warnings, laws, stories, the reader walks in under mercy.

how: Muslims recite the bismillah at the start of each surah (except at-Tawbah) and before everyday actions like eating, traveling or starting work, so ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim are names of Allah said many times a day.

o: in the name of Allah: the line over each surah
a prayer said only before eating a meal
the closing words of every Friday sermon

games.q: mercy at every door — tap the pairs.
p: the one surah without a bismillah

s: the bismillah appears 113 times in the Qur'an
it heads 113 surahs and appears again in 27:30, so 114 in all.
ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim share a root with the word for womb
r-h-m: a hadith qudsi says the womb was named from His name.
scholars agree on one reason at-Tawbah has no bismillah
a report from 'Uthman gives one reason; other scholars gave others.

games.q: the Queen of Sheba opens a letter from Sulayman. how does it begin?
o: in the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
games.why: the bismillah (27:30): the one time it appears inside a surah, which brings the count back to 114.

practice: If there's a Qur'an near you, turn a few pages just to see the line at the head of each surah.

If not, count the doors you walked through today, waking, eating, leaving the house, opening a message, and how many could have started with that line. Then, if you'd like, say it quietly now, ahead of the next one.

wordCard.voice: Bismillah. The line that opens all but one surah, appears inside a letter in surah twenty-seven, and puts the Merciful right after Allah. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: in the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

carryVoice: Your line: mercy first. Every door but one opens with it. Day six hundred seventy-eight, done.
